verdict.rationale: Viam ships its own simulation: the setup wizard can run a machine in a cloud simulated environment, Viam 101 builds a palletizing cell in simulation, and the RDK supports fake configs. Its uniform component APIs let code keep working when hardware changes in config. The evidence never explicitly says that code written against a simulated machine runs unchanged on the real robot, so sim-to-real portability is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a sim-to-real workflow with the same code, details on simulation fidelity (physics, sensors), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can run the same robot code against simulation and the real robot without a rewrite

citations.quote: the setup wizard can also run your machine in a simulated environment in the cloud, so you can start configuring and testing right away
Build a palletizing cell in simulation and learn the core concepts behind every Viam machine.
Example with a dummy configuration: `go run ./web/cmd/server -config etc/configs/fake.json`.
That means you can swap hardware without rewriting your code.
If you change a camera or motor in your config, your code keeps working.
